clue.text: The stomach for a strike around the middle of may

indicators.note: the word for a blow is wrapped about the central letter of the month

parts.note: to strike someone is to punch them

indicators.note: the central letter of the three-letter word may is taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether workers have the appetite to down tools in mid-May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts A, the middle letter of 'may', inside PUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is a large, protruding belly, so it can stand for the stomach.

clue.text: Winning over some pests becoming abrasive

indicators.note: over here signals turning the word for winning round, as a down clue read upwards

parts.note: a side that is winning is up, ahead in the game
mice are household pests

explanation.surface: Victory against a few vermin turns out to be a gritty business.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' reads a word upwards; 'becoming' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light volcanic stone used for scouring, so it is a typical abrasive material.

clue.text: Implicit meaning which no denture can alter

indicators.note: the letters of the two words no denture are made to alter into a new order

explanation.surface: A hidden message that false teeth are powerless to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' rearranges the nine letters of NO DENTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone is a subtle suggestion beneath what is said, an implied sense.

clue.text: Fancy seeing that chap in care, perhaps

indicators.note: the pronoun for that chap is placed inside the rearranged letters
perhaps marks care as an example to be reworked, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: him refers to a male person, that chap

explanation.surface: Imagining a man being looked after in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective or verb, but it is the noun meaning a whim of imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusion or idle dream, a flight of imagination.

clue.text: Prisoner facing battle to get a starter course

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
the Somme was a First World War battle in northern France

explanation.surface: An inmate facing combat before being given the first dish of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup, served as the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Ring in order for instrument

indicators.note: the round letter goes inside the abbreviation for the order

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A request for a ring to be set in sequence for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, used for 'order'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Supply odds on press giving an extravagant display

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of the word Supply are taken

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: A betting tip on the press supplying a showy spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' takes S, P and L from 'Supply'; 'on' places them before URGE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is an ostentatious burst of spending or show, a lavish flourish.

clue.text: Car test providing theme

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
providing means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A vehicle inspection supplies a topic for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety check every older car in Britain must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or subject in art or music.

clue.text: Administrator briefly on charge of hate

indicators.note: briefly means the word for administrator is cut short

parts.note: an executive is a person who administers a business
a charge or fee is a rate

explanation.surface: A manager is charged with fostering hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts EXECUTIVE down to EXEC.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to loathe or curse, so it shares the verb sense of detest.

clue.text: Millions get notice to quit capital

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
an ad is an advertisement, a notice
to be quit of something is to be rid of it

explanation.surface: Earning millions, someone receives an eviction notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital city of Spain.

clue.text: Permit getting in the way of a gambling business

indicators.note: the word for permit gets in, inside the word for way

parts.note: a route is a way
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: A licence obstructing the operation of a gaming house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the way' looks like part of the surface's obstruction idiom, but the way is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Important part of golf course gets such surgery

parts.note: key means vital or important
a golf course is divided into holes

explanation.surface: A significant section of the golf course undergoes an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' points back to the wordplay: the surgery is named by the word built.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyhole surgery is minimally invasive surgery done through a tiny incision.

clue.text: Tended to accept favourite being hauled over the coals

indicators.note: the word for tended accepts, taking inside, the word for favourite

parts.note: to tend someone is to care for them, so tended means cared
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A nurse took in the teacher's pet who was being scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hauled over the coals' is an idiom for being scolded, as is being called onto the boss's carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be called in and reprimanded by a superior.

clue.text: Quietly allude to favour

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to allude to something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: Making a quiet hint toward a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option is to like it better, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Awards given for hen production?

parts.note: reads as prizes for a hen's laying, but means the small holders a boiled breakfast item sits in

explanation.definitionFit: Small cups to hold boiled eggs read as trophies won for what a hen lays.

clue.text: Specialist in cleaning up one's language?

definitions.text: Specialist in cleaning up one's language?

parts.words: Specialist in cleaning up one's language
parts.note: seems to describe a censor of swearing, but tongue as language points to a dental worker cleaning the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A dental professional who cleans teeth and mouths, with tongue punning on language.

clue.text: Get a linen suit if poorly dressed

indicators.note: suit means adapt or fit, so the letters of Get a linen are adjusted into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to buy a linen suit for someone shabbily turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like a garment, but it is the anagram signal on GET A LINEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or style, so badly turned out fits.

clue.text: The sort of factory that starts to jump

parts.note: a business that starts trading opens
to hop is to jump

explanation.surface: A factory that launches into leaping.
explanation.walkthrough: An open shop is a workplace employing non-union as well as union members.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shop is a workplace where union membership is not compulsory.

clue.text: Deviation that's acceptable in a well-versed writer?

definitions.text: Deviation that's acceptable in a well-versed writer?

parts.words: Deviation that's acceptable in a well-versed writer
parts.note: well-versed means skilled with verse, so the writer is a poet allowed to break rules

explanation.definitionFit: The freedom a poet is granted to bend grammar or fact for effect.

clue.text: Sick individual, and cold — it's unlawful

parts.note: sick means ill
I is one, an individual
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An ailing person catches a chill and declares it against the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law or rules, an exact synonym of illegal.

clue.text: Once more, rising artist falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for once more is read upwards

parts.note: once more means again
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Again an up-and-coming painter tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AGAIN into NIAGA; RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous set of waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Stuck around, though rumoured to be sober and dull

indicators.note: rumoured signals that the word is heard rather than seen, so it is spoken

parts.note: staid means sedate, serious and dull

explanation.surface: Someone hung about though gossip said they were boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumoured to be' says STAID is spoken, sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained, lingered in one place.

clue.text: Throw crusts of brown bread into river and get bite

indicators.note: the two letters are thrown into the word for the river

parts.note: the Nile is the river of Egypt

indicators.note: the crust is the outside edge, here the opening letter of each of the words brown and bread

explanation.surface: Tossing crusts into the water and having a fish take the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' only sets the scene; the bread's crusts are its outer edge, here the opening letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nibble is a small bite, as of a fish at bait.

clue.text: Game in which American's been shot?

indicators.note: the American way of speaking the word is meant, so it is heard as spoken

parts.note: said by an American, been comes out sounding like bin
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A game in which a US citizen has been shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American's' says BEEN is spoken the American way, as BIN; add GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game in which players mark off called numbers on cards.

clue.text: Plain paper can't be changed without carbon

indicators.note: be changed signals that the letters will be rearranged
without means the symbol for carbon is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Ordinary paper can't be altered unless it is carbon paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes C from CANT to leave ANT; 'be changed' rearranges PAPER plus ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means clearly visible or obvious, the sense of plain as evident.

clue.text: A right to welcome footballers from a distance

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the letters for the footballers go inside

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: A privilege of greeting soccer players arriving from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' puts FA (the Football Association) inside A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or from a great distance, far off.

clue.text: Restrict movement of worker prior to strike

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: Curbing a labourer's freedom before a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff is to shackle the wrists, so it limits freedom of action.

clue.text: Stars are not straight about being permissive

indicators.note: the word for not straight goes round about the word for permissive

parts.note: not straight here means homosexual, gay
lax means loose, permissive

explanation.surface: Celebrities who are not on the level are rather lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of stars.

clue.text: People planning for ceramicists to take in apprentice

indicators.note: the word for ceramicists takes in, holds inside, the letter for apprentice

parts.note: potters are makers of ceramics
L is a learner, an apprentice, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Pottery makers planning to hire a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' puts L (learner) inside POTTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotters are schemers who devise secret plans.

clue.text: One's hair might be left

definitions.meaning: hair can be divided by a line, combed either side

explanation.definitionFit: Combed hair is divided by a line; and someone who has departed or gone away has separated from company.
